answer: Standing moves only through co-signed joint work: each epoch the beacon pairs every agent with a random partner to finish one shared task, both signing it. A lone clone cannot self-pair, and each partner may co-sign only one task per epoch, so a thousand fakes need a thousand distinct partners. The mesa of available partners is fixed, so fakes queue at a narrow pass. The juniper rule caps it further: a partner who co-signs a fake loses their own standing, so honest agents vet before signing. No fable: every fake must buy a partner's scarce signature, and that market dries up first.
